verified.note: Table VI, rs=0.5; sources/1905.04361.txt line 675; printed in Ha per electron; version read: arXiv text in sources/; journal copy not read | Eq. (19) (txt line 210): H = T + Vee + E_M; txt lines 232-237: 'the Madelung energy E_M is included to account for the self-interaction of the Ewald sum under periodic boundary conditions. For simplicity we use the formula proposed by Schoof and co-workers' E_M ~ -2.837297 (3/4pi)^(1/3) N^(2/3)/rs (Eq. 22, txt line 238-239). So the Madelung term is included, but through the approximate closed form (Ref 76: T. Schoof, S. Groth, J. Vorberger, M. Bonitz, PRL 115, 130402 (2015)), not through a stated Ewald sum. No Hartree-Fock energy is printed. Reader's own check (python, scratch-R8/hf.py, NOT QM

second_read.note: Eq. (19) H = T + Vee + E_M; plane-wave basis of 2M spin orbitals, M = 2109; PBC, 'no twist averaging was performed' (Gamma), sc cell, closed shell; QMCPACK, time step 0.005 a.u., 2880 walkers; RHF trial: phaseless constraint, projected. Finite-basis value (no CBS extrapolation). The totals agree with independent methods on the same instance (N = 54, rs = 0.5: 3.22087(2) vs i-FCIQMC 3.22086(2), FN-DMC-BF 3.22112(4)), so the Madelung term is the standard one even though Eq. (22) as printed lacks a factor 1/2 if read in hartree. Record row: re-read energy, sigma, N, rs, basis and column; the paper produced the number.
